sections.content: Norfolk, Virginia doesn't always make the headlines the way Atlanta or Phoenix do. But for real estate investors who know where to look, it offers something rare: a stable, military-backed economy, growing rental demand, and home prices that are still accessible compared to most major metros. Whether you're brand new to the game — in which case check out this guide to Real Estate Investing for Beginners — or you're an experienced investor expanding into new markets, Norfolk deserves a serious look. This guide walks you through everything you need to know to find and close profitable real estate deals in Norfolk VA.
Norfolk VA Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Norfolk is the second-largest city in Virginia and sits at the heart of the Hampton Roads metro area, which includes Virginia Beach, Chesapeake, Portsmouth, and Suffolk. Together, this metro houses roughly 1.8 million people. The region's economy is anchored by Naval Station Norfolk, the largest naval base in the world, employing over 80,000 military and civilian personnel. That single fact transforms the investment thesis for this market: you have a constant, rotating population of renters with steady government paychecks who need housing near the base.

Beyond the military, Norfolk is home to Old Dominion University, Sentara Healthcare, and a growing tech sector driven by federal contracting. The city has also invested heavily in its downtown waterfront, the Ghent arts district, and light rail expansion. These are the kinds of fundamentals that support long-term property values, not just short-term speculation.
Norfolk Home Prices: What Are You Actually Looking At?

As of 2024, the median home price in Norfolk sits around $285,000 to $310,000 depending on the neighborhood and property type. That's well below the national median of approximately $420,000, which means your capital goes further here. Single-family rentals in mid-tier neighborhoods typically rent for $1,400 to $1,900 per month, giving investors a realistic shot at the 1% rule in certain zip codes. Distressed properties — the bread and butter of wholesalers and flippers — can be found in the $100,000 to $180,000 range, with after-repair values (ARVs) often landing between $220,000 and $290,000. That spread is where the money is made. Use our free ARV Calculator to quickly estimate after-repair value before making any offer.

Pro Tip: In Norfolk, military housing allowances (BAH rates) for E-5 and above servicemembers often exceed $1,800/month. Pricing your rental at or just below the BAH rate for your area makes your property instantly attractive to military tenants, who tend to pay on time and take care of their housing.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Norfolk VA
Not all of Norfolk's 65-plus neighborhoods offer the same opportunity. Here's a breakdown of the areas that consistently attract investor activity across different strategies.
Wards Corner and Norview: Value-Add and Rental Plays

Located in the northern part of the city, Wards Corner and Norview offer some of Norfolk's most affordable entry points. Home prices here frequently fall in the $130,000 to $200,000 range, and rental demand is consistent thanks to proximity to the naval base and easy highway access. These neighborhoods are ideal for buy-and-hold investors and wholesalers looking for motivated sellers in working-class areas.
Ghent and Colonial Place: Flip-Friendly with Strong ARVs

Ghent is Norfolk's most desirable urban neighborhood — a walkable, arts-forward area with historic bungalows, local restaurants, and a strong owner-occupant buyer pool. Fully renovated homes here regularly sell for $350,000 to $450,000, creating healthy flip margins when you can acquire distressed properties at the right price. Colonial Place, just east of Ghent, offers similar demographics with slightly lower entry costs. These are competitive areas, so speed and solid comps matter. Before running numbers on any deal here, use the free Deal Calculator to make sure your offer leaves room for profit.
Campostella and Berkley: Emerging Markets with High Upside

These south Norfolk neighborhoods are still early in their revitalization cycle. Prices are low — often under $160,000 — but proximity to downtown and ongoing city investment make them worth watching. Investors with a longer time horizon and a tolerance for a bit more risk may find significant upside as gentrification continues moving south from downtown.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Norfolk VA

items: Wholesale deals: Norfolk's aging housing stock and high percentage of absentee landlords create consistent motivated seller leads. Probate properties, pre-foreclosures, and tax-delinquent homes are reliable sources. If you're new to this strategy, start with our guide to Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners.

Fix-and-flip: The renovation-to-resale cycle works well in transitional neighborhoods like Ghent, Colonial Place, and the areas around ODU. Strong buyer demand from military families and young professionals supports a healthy resale market.

Buy-and-hold rentals: Military tenant demand makes Norfolk one of the more reliable rental markets in the South. Single-family homes near the base and along transit corridors perform particularly well.

BRRRR strategy: Buy, Rehab, Rent, Refinance, Repeat — this method thrives in Norfolk because you can acquire discounted properties, force equity through renovation, and pull capital back out through a cash-out refi while keeping a performing rental asset.
Short-term rentals: Areas near the beach, the Naro cinema district, and the waterfront attract Airbnb traffic, though you'll want to check current city regulations before pursuing this strategy.

sections.content: Norfolk Real Estate Market Trends You Need to Know

Norfolk's market has shown steady appreciation of 5% to 8% annually over the past several years, outperforming many comparable second-tier cities. Inventory remains tight — typically running 1.5 to 2.5 months of supply in desirable neighborhoods — which supports prices and helps investors resell renovated homes quickly. Rising interest rates have pushed some would-be buyers back into the rental market, actually strengthening demand for investor-owned rentals. One headwind to watch: parts of Norfolk face flooding risk due to sea-level rise, and some coastal areas are seeing rising insurance costs. Always check flood zone maps before acquiring property in low-lying areas near the Elizabeth River or the Chesapeake Bay waterfront.

"The markets that create generational wealth for investors aren't always the flashiest ones. They're the ones with stable employment, consistent rental demand, and prices that still make the numbers work. Norfolk checks every one of those boxes." — Common wisdom among Hampton Roads investment community
How to Find Off-Market Deals in Norfolk VA

The best real estate deals in Norfolk VA rarely show up on the MLS. To find real opportunities, you need to go off-market. Direct mail campaigns targeting absentee owners, tax-delinquent properties, and probate leads are all effective strategies in this city. Driving for dollars in Norview, Campostella, and Wards Corner can surface vacant and distressed properties before anyone else knows about them. Building relationships with local probate attorneys, estate sale companies, and property managers also opens doors to deals that never hit the open market. For a complete breakdown of these tactics, read our guide on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals.
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Looking at Norfolk

Norfolk is an accessible market for remote investors, but you need the right team on the ground. Start by identifying a local investor-friendly real estate agent who understands ARV-based pricing, not just retail comps. Connect with a property manager who has experience with military tenants — they'll know how to handle PCS move-outs (Permanent Change of Station) and maintain occupancy through tenant turnover. Find a reliable general contractor before you need one; good GCs in the Hampton Roads area stay busy, so build that relationship early.

items: Join the Hampton Roads Real Estate Investors Association (HREIA) to network with local wholesalers, agents, and contractors.
Pull city permit records to identify recent renovation activity — where investors are working tells you where the deals are moving.
Order a home inspection even on wholesale deals when possible. Norfolk's older housing stock (much of it built pre-1960) can carry significant deferred maintenance costs.
Check Norfolk's zoning maps for ADU (accessory dwelling unit) opportunities — some lots allow you to add a second unit, dramatically improving cash flow.
Always underwrite for flood insurance separately if the property is in a FEMA Zone AE or VE — it can add $2,000 to $5,000 annually to your holding costs.

Is Norfolk VA the Right Market for You?

If you're looking for a market with affordable entry points, stable military-backed rental demand, and real room to force equity through renovation, Norfolk VA deserves a spot on your shortlist. It won't make you rich overnight, but the fundamentals are sound, the deal flow is consistent, and the competition — while growing — hasn't yet reached the saturation levels of larger Sun Belt metros. The investors winning in Norfolk right now are the ones who do their homework, build solid local teams, and move quickly when the numbers make sense.
